data.name: Raghukul
data.gender_notes: Raghukul is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Raghukul refers to the lineage or dynasty of King Raghu, an ancient king in Hindu mythology known for his generosity and righteousness. The name Raghukul carries the meaning “Descendant of Raghu” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Raghukul usually hope their child will grow to embody descendant of raghu and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodying the virtues of a noble lineage
data.etymology: Raghukul belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Descendant of Raghu.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Raghukul total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Raghukul holds great cultural significance in India as it is closely associated with the epic Ramayana, one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India. The story of Ramayana revolves around Prince Rama, who is the sixth incarnation of Lord Vishnu and part of the Raghukul lineage. The narrative is deeply influenced by Indian culture and values, portraying the importance of righteousness, loyalty, and family in Hindu society.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Raghukul carries spiritual significance as it is linked to the divine descent of King Rama, the embodiment of virtue, truth, and morality. The legacy of Raghukul serves as a reminder of the transcendental nature of dharma and the importance of maintaining moral virtues in every aspect of life. It also underscores the idea that everyone is interconnected, as they belong to the same universal family or kul. This belief inspires selfless acts and oneness amongst individuals.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Raghukul carries the symbolism of the illustrious Raghu Dynasty, representing strength, wisdom, and righteousness. It is a spiritual reminder to uphold these virtues and continue the legacy of Raghu's noble lineage.

vedic_reference.note: Not from Vedas or Upanishads, but from Hindu mythology.

historical_references.reference: Raghukula Gita is an ancient Indian text, a part of the Mahabharata, which describes the origin and genealogy of the Raghukula or the Ikshvaku dynasty, tracing it back to Lord Rama. The text holds significant importance in Hindu mythology and is considered a sacred scripture.

The Raghukula Bhagavatam is a 16th century Sanskrit literary work by Bhikhan Ram, a Jain ascetic, who wrote it under the inspiration of the 23rd Tirthankara, Sambhavanatha. The work comprises 12,000 verses and provides a detailed account of the life stories of the Raghukula kings from Ikshvaku to Rama.
